If the value of for example `create` is `true`, then the token can create rows in all tables related to the workspace. If a list is provided with for example `[["table", 1]]` then the token only has create permissions for the table with id 1. slug.description: The slug of the user template to download.

revision_id.description: The id of the revision of the user template that the user was shown. Its owner and the instance admins may download any revision. Anyone else downloads the public revision, or the latest one of a template that isn't public with the token of its private link.

skip_files.description: If true, then the files are not downloaded and imported.

table_id.description: The ID of the table to duplicate.

AIProviderFeatureSettingStateEnum.description: * `configured` - configured * `inherited` - inherited * `overridden` - overridden * `disabled` - disabled * `unconfigured` - unconfigured * `invalid` - invalid

feature_types.description: The AI features allowed to select this model. This controls eligibility, not which features currently use the model.

Account.description: This serializer must be kept in sync with `UserSerializer`.

language.description: An ISO 639 language code (with optional variant) selected by the user. Ex: en-GB.

email_notification_frequency.description: The maximum frequency at which the user wants to receive email notifications. * `instant` - instant * `daily` - daily * `weekly` - weekly * `never` - never

completed_onboarding.description: Indicates whether the user has completed the onboarding.

completed_guided_tours.description: Indicates which guided tour types have been completed.

ActionScopes.description: Mixin to a DRF serializer class to raise an exception if data with unknown fields is provided to the serializer.

root.description: If set to true then actions registered in the root scope will be included when undoing or redoing.

workspace.description: If set to a workspaces id then any actions directly related to that workspace will be be included when undoing or redoing.

all_workspaces.description: If set to true then actions registered in the workspace scope of every workspace the user is a member of will be included when undoing or redoing.

application.description: If set to an applications id then any actions directly related to that application will be be included when undoing or redoing.

table.description: If set to a table id then any actions directly related to that table will be be included when undoing or redoing.

view.description: If set to an view id then any actions directly related to that view will be be included when undoing or redoing.

page.description: If set to a page id then any actions directly related to that page will be included when undoing or redoing.

shared_page.description: If set to a shared page id then any actions related to that builder's shared elements will be included when undoing or redoing.

workflow.description: If set to a workflow id then any actions directly related to that workflow will be be included when undoing or redoing.

teams_in_workspace.description: If set to a workspace id then any actions directly related to that workspace will be be included when undoing or redoing.

AdminUserTemplate.description: A row of the admin page.

revision_id.description: The id of the serialized revision. Sent with an install, so that the template isn't installed if it was updated since.

type.description: Whether it's an official or a user template.

icon.description: The icon class name that can be used for displaying purposes.

workspace_id.description: The group containing the applications related to the template. The read endpoints related to that group are publicly accessible for preview purposes. Revisions of the same template that only differ in their details share it.

open_application.description: The application ID that must be opened when the template is previewed. If null, then the first will automatically be chosen.

author.description: The author of the template. Null if they were deleted.

state.description: The tab of the admin page the template is on. * `private` - Private * `in_review` - In review * `rejected` - Rejected * `blocked` - Blocked * `public` - Public

reason.description: Why an admin rejected or blocked the template, for a rejected or blocked one.

listed.description: Whether a revision of the template is listed for everybody, also while a later one is in review or rejected.

private_link.description: Whether the private link of the template is on. The link itself is never shown.

can_approve.description: Whether an admin can approve the revision: in review or rejected, with content, and not edited since it was submitted.

edited_since_submitted.description: Whether the template was edited since the revision was submitted, which is why an admin can't approve it.

updated_since_blocked.description: Whether the latest revision was made after the template was blocked; false outside the blocked tab.

can_reject.description: Whether an admin can reject the template: in review, or listed.

reject_unlists.description: Whether rejecting the template takes it out of the listing: when it's listed, unless only its edit is in review.

reviewed_on.description: When an admin, or a submit without review, last reviewed the revision. Null if never.

install_count.description: How many times the template was installed.

submitted_on.description: When the revision was submitted for review, if it was.

public.description: The listed templates without an edit in review or rejected.

slug.description: The unique slug where the view can be accessed publicly on.

public.description: Indicates whether the view is publicly accessible to visitors.

ownership_type.description: Indicates how the access to the view is determined. By default, views are collaborative and shared for all users that have access to the table.

workspace.description: The workspace that the application belongs to.

last_viewed.description: When the requesting user last opened something in this application, or null if never. Only present in responses to a user.

pending_count.description: How many things in this application wait for the requesting user to act, such as tool calls to approve. Only present in responses to a user.

readiness.description: Whether the agent's configuration is complete and its model is enabled.

reasoning_effort.description: How much the model reasons before it replies. Null uses the model's default. * `off` - off * `low` - low * `medium` - medium * `high` - high

applied_reasoning_effort.description: The reasoning effort replies use with the selected model: the chosen one, or the next higher one the model accepts. Null means replies use the model's default, because none is chosen, the model doesn't accept one, or the model isn't available. * `off` - off * `low` - low * `medium` - medium * `high` - high

run_as.description: The configured identity and its active, trashed or missing status. Null means no workspace access was selected.

allowed_tools.description: The names of the tools the agent may call while it has an identity to act as.

ask_first_tools.description: The names of the allowed tools that wait for the conversation owner's approval before they run.

available_tools.description: Every tool an agent can be allowed to call, with its group and whether it changes data.

web_search_enabled.description: Whether the agent may search the web through its AI provider.

web_search_available.description: Whether the agent's model may try to search the web. Its provider can still refuse a search, which the reply then shows.

web_search_blocked_by_tools.description: Whether the agent's model can search the web, but not while the agent uses workspace tools.

web_fetch_enabled.description: Whether the agent may open web pages, which Baserow fetches.

available_trigger_types.description: The trigger types that can be added to the agent on this instance, as service type names.

available_action_types.description: The service types available as configured agent actions.

max_actions.description: How many actions the agent can have on this instance. Null is no limit.

max_queued_trigger_runs.description: How many runs of a trigger that waits or runs in parallel can be queued on this instance; later firings are skipped. 0 or less is no limit.

max_parallel_trigger_runs.description: How many runs of a trigger that runs in parallel can go at once on this instance; later firings are queued. 0 or less is no limit.

run_id.description: The run writing a reply in this conversation, or null.

pending_approval_count.description: The number of held tool calls in this conversation waiting for a decision.

shared.description: Whether a trigger started this conversation. A shared conversation is read by everyone who may read the agent's conversations, accepts no messages, and its held tool calls are decided by anyone who may send the agent messages.

trigger_id.description: The trigger that started this conversation, or null.

trigger_type.description: The service type of the trigger that started this conversation, such as periodic, or null.

trigger_name.description: The current name of the trigger that started this conversation, blank when it shows its type's default, or null.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page, `null` when no more conversations follow.

run_id.description: The run writing this reply, to follow its output: set while it runs and in the response that started it.

approvals.description: The reply's held tool calls, joined to their steps by step_id, with the decision on each.

AgentMessageStatusEnum.description: * `queued` - Queued * `running` - Running * `completed` - Completed * `cancelled` - Cancelled * `failed` - Failed * `waiting` - Waiting

item.description: The failed item's name or ID.

AgentMessageStepStatusEnum.description: * `running` - running * `waiting` - waiting * `done` - done * `failed` - failed * `rejected` - rejected * `stopped` - stopped * `skipped` - skipped

AgentRunAsOption.description: A selectable identity returned by the Agent's scoped run-as endpoint.

deactivated.description: Whether the Agent's workspace can't use the tool, for lack of a licence for example. A deactivated tool can't be allowed.

pause.description: Which pause of its reply held the call, counting from 1.

AgentToolDecision.description: Mixin to a DRF serializer class to raise an exception if data with unknown fields is provided to the serializer.

id.description: The id of a pending approval.

approved.description: Whether the held call may run. A rejected call never runs.

reason.description: Why the call is rejected, passed on to the agent. Only accepted with a rejection.

AgentTrigger.description: A trigger with its service, whose schema describes its payload, and message.

type.description: The service type of the trigger.

name.description: The trigger's name, trimmed. Blank shows a default worded by its type, such as its schedule.

message.description: The formula, resolved against the trigger's payload, whose text opens each conversation the trigger starts. Empty opens it with the payload itself.

on_overlap.description: What a firing does while a reply of the trigger is still going: `skip` starts nothing, `wait` queues its conversation until that reply ends, `parallel` starts it alongside, up to a cap, then queues it. * `skip` - Skip * `wait` - Wait for the previous run * `parallel` - Run in parallel

batch_size.description: How many records of a list payload, such as created rows, each conversation receives: a larger event starts one conversation per batch. Payloads that aren't lists ignore it.

service.description: The service producing the trigger's events.

last_fired_on.description: When a firing last started or queued a conversation.

last_skipped_on.description: When a firing was last skipped.

last_skipped_reason.description: Why the last skipped firing started nothing, empty until one is. * `rate_limited` - Rate limited * `agent_rate_limited` - Agent rate limited * `previous_running` - Previous run still going * `queue_full` - Queue full * `no_access` - No access * `event_too_large` - Event too large

AgentTriggerType.description: A trigger type the agent may use, as the agent's run identity sees it.

type.description: The service type, one of the configuration's available_trigger_types.

form_choices.description: What the type's form may choose from for the agent's run identity, such as `databases` with the tables it can read, or null when the form needs nothing.

default_on_overlap.description: The overlap rule a new trigger of this type gets when none is given. * `skip` - Skip * `wait` - Wait for the previous run * `parallel` - Run in parallel

AggregationRawTypeEnum.description: * `empty_count` - empty_count * `not_empty_count` - not_empty_count * `unique_count` - unique_count * `min` - min * `max` - max * `sum` - sum * `average` - average * `median` - median * `decile` - decile * `variance` - variance * `std_dev` - std_dev * `distribution` - distribution

message_id.description: The ID of the message that was cancelled.

code.description: A short error code that can be used to identify the error.

id.description: The unique ID of the message.

content.description: The content of the AI message.

sources.description: The list of relevant source URLs referenced in the knowledge. Can be empty or null.

onboarding_target.description: The table created during onboarding, opened when the run ends.

can_submit_feedback.description: Whether the user can submit feedback for this message. Only true for messages with an associated prediction.

human_sentiment.description: The sentiment for the message, if it has been rated. * `LIKE` - LIKE * `DISLIKE` - DISLIKE

run_status.description: How the run that wrote this message ended when it didn't complete: `cancelled` or `failed`. Null for a complete answer.

error_code.description: Why that run failed or stopped: `interrupted`, `not_started`, `timeout`, `failed`, `model_unavailable` or `access_lost`.

content.description: The reasoning content of the AI message.

message_id.description: The ID of the message being generated.

content.description: The message to show while the AI is thinking

type.description: The type of the job.

progress_percentage.description: A percentage indicating how far along the job is. 100 means that it's finished.

state.description: Indicates the state of the import job.

human_readable_error.description: A human readable error message indicating what went wrong.

error_code.description: A machine readable error code indicating why the job failed.

workspace_id.description: The workspace ID where the Airtable base must be imported into.

airtable_share_id.description: Public ID of the shared Airtable base or view that must be imported.

skip_files.description: If true, then the files are not downloaded and imported.

has_workflow_actions.description: Whether the field has any configured actions. The client uses this to decide whether a cell renders a button that dispatches actions or an inert one.

requires_reconfiguration.description: Whether a click is sure to fail, because an action points at a table, field or integration that is in the trash or gone, updates a row without saying which, or sends an email to nobody. The client renders a disabled button with a warning instead.

opens_new_tab.description: Whether an action opens a URL in a new tab. The client then opens the tab as the button is clicked, because a browser may block one opened after the click's request returns.

semantic_search_enabled.description: Whether the field's values can be searched by their meaning.

semantic_search_status.description: The state of the semantic search index of the field: `indexing`, `ready`, `error`, `incompatible` if a change of another field made its value something else than text, `paused` if the workspace doesn't have the required license or `unavailable` if the instance doesn't support it. immutable_type.description: Indicates whether the field type is immutable. If true, then it won't be possible to change the field type via the API.

immutable_properties.description: Indicates whether the field properties are immutable. If true, then it won't be possible to change the properties and the type via the API.

database_id.description: The ID of the database this field belongs to.

workspace_id.description: The ID of the workspace this field belongs to.

db_index.description: If true, then an index will be added to the Baserow field to increase lookup and filter speed. Note that this comes at a performance cost when creating the row and updating the cell.

field_constraints.description: The constraints applied to this field.

related_fields.description: A list of related fields which also changed.

date_include_time.description: Indicates if the field also includes a time.

date_show_tzinfo.description: Indicates if the timezone should be shown.

date_force_timezone.description: Force a timezone for the field overriding user profile settings.

semantic_search_enabled.description: Whether the field's values can be searched by their meaning.

semantic_search_status.description: The state of the semantic search index of the field: `indexing`, `ready`, `error`, `incompatible` if a change of another field made its value something else than text, `paused` if the workspace doesn't have the required license or `unavailable` if the instance doesn't support it. labels.description: A formula resolving to the graph labels.

series.description: The series shown in the graph.

width.description: The width of the table field in the related view.

hidden.description: Whether or not the field should be hidden in the current view.

order.description: The position that the field has within the view, lowest first. If there is another field with the same order value then the field with the lowest id must be shown first.

aggregation_type.description: Indicates how the field value is aggregated. This value is different from the `aggregation_raw_type`. The `aggregation_raw_type` is the value extracted from the database, while the `aggregation_type` can implies further calculations. For example: if you want to compute an average, `sum` is going to be the `aggregation_raw_type`, the value extracted from database, and `sum / row_count` will be the aggregation result displayed to the user. This aggregation_type should be used by the client to compute the final value.

aggregation_raw_type.description: Indicates how to compute the raw aggregation value from database. This type must be registered in the backend prior to use it. * `empty_count` - empty_count * `not_empty_count` - not_empty_count * `unique_count` - unique_count * `min` - min * `max` - max * `sum` - sum * `average` - average * `median` - median * `decile` - decile * `variance` - variance * `std_dev` - std_dev * `distribution` - distribution

truncated.description: Whether descendant loading stopped early because the response page or group cap was reached.

aggregations.description: Table-level field aggregation totals keyed by field db_column, mirroring the grid view field-aggregations response. Only present when `include_totals=true` was requested.

path.description: Mapping of group-by field db_column names to the serialized group value at every depth from 0 up to this group's depth.

display.description: Mapping of group-by field db_column names to the renderable display value for reference fields (for example collaborator names or the linked row's primary value). Only present for fields whose group value is an id or list of ids that the client cannot render on its own.

depth.description: Zero-based depth of this group in the group-by hierarchy.

row_count.description: Number of leaf rows descending from this group. In `aggregations_only` mode, this is still returned so derived aggregation values can be formatted without using optimistic client-side counts.

children_count.description: Number of immediate sub-groups. Omitted at leaf depth.

sibling_index.description: Zero-based index of this group among its siblings. Omitted in `aggregations_only` mode, which returns no windowed layout.

row_offset.description: Absolute offset of this group's first descendant row in the full grouped row order. Omitted in `aggregations_only` mode, which returns no windowed layout.

aggregations.description: Per-group aggregation values keyed by field db_column, mirroring the grid view field-aggregations response. Only present for visible fields that have a scalar aggregation configured.

parent.description: The serialized parent group path requested for this page.

filter_type.description: Indicates whether all the rows should apply to all filters (AND) or to any filter (OR). * `AND` - And * `OR` - Or

filters_disabled.description: Allows users to see results unfiltered while still keeping the filters saved for the view.

public_view_has_password.description: Indicates whether the public view is password protected or not. :return: True if the public view is password protected, False otherwise.

allow_public_export.description: Indicates whether it's allowed to export a publicly shared view.

frozen_column_count.description: Number of frozen columns including the primary field.

group_by_layout.description: How grouped rows are presented: sections with a header above each group, or one column per group-by level beside the rows. * `section` - Section * `column` - Column

public.description: Indicates whether the view is publicly accessible to visitors.

slug.description: The unique slug that can be used to construct a public URL.

table_id.description: The table where the data is synced into.

last_sync.description: Timestamp when the table was last synced.

auto_add_new_properties.description: If enabled and new properties are detected on sync, then they're automatically added. Note that this means all properties will always be added.

delete_unmatched_rows.description: If enabled, rows that are no longer present in the source are deleted from the synced table on every sync. If disabled, those rows are kept and reused if the matching source row reappears.

two_way_sync.description: If enabled, then it's possible to make changes to the synced table. They will automatically be synced with the source data. Note that this is only possible if the data sync type has a two-way sync strategy.

jira_url.description: The base URL of your Jira instance (e.g., https://your-domain.atlassian.net).

jira_project_key.description: The project key of the Jira project (e.g., PROJ).

jira_username.description: The username of the Jira account used to authenticate. Is only used if the `jira_authentication` is equal `API_TOKEN`

rows.description: Every select option related to the view's single select field can have its own entry like this.

count.description: The total count of rows that are included in this group.

results.description: All the rows that belong in this group related with the provided `limit` and `offset`.

hidden.description: Whether or not the field should be hidden in the card.

order.description: The order that the field has in the view. Lower value is first.

filter_type.description: Indicates whether all the rows should apply to all filters (AND) or to any filter (OR). * `AND` - And * `OR` - Or

filters_disabled.description: Allows users to see results unfiltered while still keeping the filters saved for the view.

public_view_has_password.description: Indicates whether the public view is password protected or not. :return: True if the public view is password protected, False otherwise.

allow_public_export.description: Indicates whether it's allowed to export a publicly shared view.

card_cover_image_field.description: References a file field of which the first image must be shown as card cover image.

public.description: Indicates whether the view is publicly accessible to visitors.

slug.description: The unique slug that can be used to construct a public URL.

Template.description: Serializes a template revision. The id, slug and keywords are the template's, so they are read from its root.

revision_id.description: The id of the serialized revision. Sent with an install, so that the template isn't installed if it was updated since.

type.description: Whether it's an official or a user template.

icon.description: The icon class name that can be used for displaying purposes.

workspace_id.description: The group containing the applications related to the template. The read endpoints related to that group are publicly accessible for preview purposes. Revisions of the same template that only differ in their details share it.

is_default.description: Indicates if the template must be selected by default. The web-frontend automatically selects the first `is_default` template that it can find.

open_application.description: The application ID that must be opened when the template is previewed. If null, then the first will automatically be chosen.

author_name.description: The first name of the author of a user template. Null for an official template or a deleted author.

url.description: The URL of the archive, which imports like a workspace export.

file_name.description: The name to save the archive as.

user_selectable.description: Whether authors can put their user templates in this category. Some are reserved for official templates.
Whether authors can put their user templates in this category. Some are reserved for official templates.

TemplateListItem.description: A revision of a template in the flat list, or opened by its slug. The fields marked as only shown to the owner of a user template are null for anyone else.

revision_id.description: The id of the serialized revision. Sent with an install, so that the template isn't installed if it was updated since.

type.description: Whether it's an official or a user template.

icon.description: The icon class name that can be used for displaying purposes.

workspace_id.description: The group containing the applications related to the template. The read endpoints related to that group are publicly accessible for preview purposes. Revisions of the same template that only differ in their details share it.

is_default.description: Indicates if the template must be selected by default. The web-frontend automatically selects the first `is_default` template that it can find.

open_application.description: The application ID that must be opened when the template is previewed. If null, then the first will automatically be chosen.

author_name.description: The first name of the author of a user template. Null for an official template or a deleted author.

is_own.description: Whether the authenticated user owns this user template.

updated_on.description: When the content shown was last changed: the creation of the revision of a user template, the last update of an official one.

state.description: The state of the template as shown to its owner, and to instance admins on the template page. Null for anyone else.

reason.description: Why the template was rejected or blocked, if given. Only shown to its owner, and to instance admins on the template page.

can_make_public.description: Whether making the template public lists it or sends it to review: it's not blocked, in review, or listed as it is. Only shown to its owner, null on listed rows.

make_public_needs_review.description: Whether making the template public sends it to the review of an instance admin, because approval is required or an admin rejected it since it was last approved. Only shown to its owner, null on listed rows.

update_needs_review.description: Whether an update of the template sends it to the review of an instance admin: when it's listed and approval is required or an admin rejected it since it was last approved, or when it's in review already. Only shown to its owner.

listed.description: Whether a revision of the template is listed for everybody, also while a later one is in review or rejected. Only shown to its owner, and to instance admins on the template page.

source_workspace_id.description: The workspace the applications of the latest revision were copied from, if known. Only shown to its owner.

source_application_ids.description: The applications the latest revision was copied from. Only shown to its owner.

install_count.description: How many times the template was installed. Only shown to its owner.

private_link_token.description: The token of the private link, null without one. Only shown to its owner.

primary.description: Indicates if the field is a primary field. If `true` the field cannot be deleted and the value should represent the whole row.

read_only.description: Indicates whether the field is a read only field. If true, it's not possible to update the cell value.

immutable_type.description: Indicates whether the field type is immutable. If true, then it won't be possible to change the field type via the API.

immutable_properties.description: Indicates whether the field properties are immutable. If true, then it won't be possible to change the properties and the type via the API.

database_id.description: The ID of the database this field belongs to.

workspace_id.description: The ID of the workspace this field belongs to.

db_index.description: If true, then an index will be added to the Baserow field to increase lookup and filter speed. Note that this comes at a performance cost when creating the row and updating the cell.

field_constraints.description: The constraints applied to this field.

text_default.description: If set, this value is going to be added every time a new row created.

semantic_search_enabled.description: Whether the field's values can be searched by their meaning.

semantic_search_status.description: The state of the semantic search index of the field: `indexing`, `ready`, `error`, `incompatible` if a change of another field made its value something else than text, `paused` if the workspace doesn't have the required license or `unavailable` if the instance doesn't support it. Null if semantic search is disabled.

name.description: The human readable name of the database token for the user.

workspace.description: Only the tables of the workspace can be accessed.

key.description: The unique token key that can be used to authorize for the table row endpoints.

permissions.description: Indicates per operation which permissions the database token has within the whole workspace. If the value of for example `create` is `true`, then the token can create rows in all tables related to the workspace. If a list is provided with for example `[["table", 1]]` then the token only has create permissions for the table with id 1. Same goes for if a database references is provided. `[['database', 1]]` means create permissions for all tables in the database with id 1. Example: ```json { "create": true// Allows creating rows in all tables. // Allows reading rows from database 1 and table 10. "read": [["database", 1], ["table", 10]], "update": false // Denies updating rows in all tables. "delete": [] // Denies deleting rows in all tables. } ```

anyOf.description: Indicating if the database token has permissions to all tables.
First element should indicate the reference type `database` or `table`.
Second element should indicate the ID of the reference.
